question:
A 37-year-old woman comes for a follow-up prenatal visit at 18 weeks' gestation. At 12 weeks' gestation, ultrasonography showed increased nuchal translucency and pregnancy-associated plasma protein A (PAPP-A) was decreased by 2 standard deviations. Chorionic villus sampling showed a 47, XX karyotype. During this visit, ultrasonography shows a hypoplastic nasal bone, shortened femur length, shortened middle phalanges of the fifth digits with clinodactyly. A quadruple marker test would most likely show which of the following sets of findings?
 $$$ α-Fetoprotein (AFP) %%% Estriol %%% β-Human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG) %%% Inhibin A $$$?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Increased nuchal translucency -> Decreased PAPP-A -> Suggestive of chromosomal abnormalities -> Chorionic villus sampling shows 47, XX karyotype -> Indicates Down syndrome (Trisomy 21) -> Associated with decreased AFP and estriol -> Increased β-HCG and inhibin A -> Likely quadruple marker test results: ↓ ↓ ↑ ↑ -> 85%

CHAIN: Increased nuchal translucency -> Decreased PAPP-A -> Risk for aneuploidy confirmed by karyotype -> 47, XX indicates Down syndrome -> Hypoplastic nasal bone and shortened femur length observed -> Associated with abnormal quadruple marker test results -> Decreased AFP and estriol levels expected -> Increased β-HCG and inhibin A levels expected -> Likely quadruple marker test results: ↓ ↓ ↑ ↑ -> 80%

CHAIN: Increased nuchal translucency -> Decreased PAPP-A -> Suggestive of potential Down syndrome -> Karyotype confirms 47, XX -> Physical findings consistent with Down syndrome -> Quadruple marker test typically shows decreased AFP and estriol -> Increased β-HCG and inhibin A levels -> Likely quadruple marker test results: ↓ ↓ ↑ ↑ -> 75%
analysis: The clinical scenario describes a 37-year-old woman with findings suggestive of Down syndrome (Trisomy 21), including increased nuchal translucency, decreased PAPP-A, hypoplastic nasal bone, and shortened femur length. In pregnancies affected by Down syndrome, the quadruple marker test typically shows decreased levels of α-Fetoprotein (AFP), Estriol, and Inhibin A, while β-Human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG) is usually elevated. Therefore, the most likely set of findings for this patient would be decreased AFP, decreased Estriol, increased HCG, and increased Inhibin A. This aligns with option opb (↓ ↓ ↑ ↑).
